title: Evidence for a jet and outflow from Sgr A*: a continuum and spectral line study
question: To establish if there is a collimated jet and outflow arising from Sgr A* by studying its environment using sub-arcsecond hydrogen recombination line and broad-band radio continuum observations.

what.value: Upper limit on Br-gamma emission within 0.2'' of Sgr A* of ~ 2 Jy km s^-1

evidence.quote: The upper limit on the Brγ emission within 0.2′′ of Sgr A* is ∼ 2 Jy km s−1 (Ciurlo et al. 2020).

what.value: Br-gamma emissivity for Te ~ 10^4 K and ne ~ 10^4 cm^-3 of j_gamma ~ 2.7 x 10^-28 erg s^-1 cm^-3 sr^-1

evidence.quote: The Brγ emissivity for Te ∼ 104 K and ne ∼ 104 cm−3 is jγ ∼ 2.7 × 10−28 erg s−1 cm−3 sr−1 (Hummer and Storey 1987).

what.value: Rotation measure detected toward Sgr A* (RM ~ -5 x 10^5 rad m^-2)

evidence.quote: One of the implications of the presence of ionized gas on such a small scale associated with Sgr A* is that it can also explain the large rotation measure detected toward Sgr A* (RM∼−5 × 105 rad m−2) (Bower et al. 2018).

recipe.goal: Self-calibrate and image ALMA and VLA recombination line cubes without uv-plane continuum subtraction
recipe.method: Combine or split spectral windows, perform iterative phase (and for Band 6, final amplitude and phase) self-calibration on Sgr A*, and image line cubes directly prior to continuum subtraction.
key_parameters: H30a channel width 45 km s^-1 from -3770 to +700 km s^-1; H39a channel width 15.625 MHz; VLA H52a and H56a channel width 2 MHz

recipe.goal: Extract spectra toward Sgr A*, equalize flux across spectral windows, and subtract continuum in the image plane
recipe.method: Extract spectrum in aperture centered on Sgr A*, equalize adjacent spectral windows by taking the ratio of mean fluxes in edge channels (5 channels for ALMA H30a, 10 channels for VLA H52a/H56a) and scaling, concatenate spws, and subtract a linear continuum fit over selected line-free velocity intervals.
key_parameters: Extraction apertures: inner 0.23'' (or 0.46'' diameter) for H30a, inner 0.75'' (or 1.5'') for H39a, 0.20'' x 0.11'' for H52a, 0.22'' x 0.27'' for H56a; scaling factor 1.0052 for H30a lower velocity window, 0.9832 to 1.003 for H52a
assumptions: Selected velocity ranges at band edges are sufficiently free of line emission to define a linear continuum

recipe.goal: Map spatial distribution of extreme velocity (-2500 and +4000 km s^-1) ionized gas
recipe.method: Select spectral windows containing -2500 and 4000 km s^-1 emission, make moment/average maps of 5 channels near low and high velocity band edges (channels 5-10 and 50-55), and subtract them from each other to form continuum-subtracted line emission contour maps.
key_parameters: Channels 5-10 and 50-55 in spectral windows covering -2500 and 4000 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Image multi-band VLA radio continuum from 1 to 48 GHz to identify persistent jet and outflow structures
recipe.method: Self-calibrate VLA A-array broadband visibility data in phase and amplitude on Sgr A*, split bandwidth into multiple channels to account for frequency response, and construct high-dynamic-range continuum images and spectral channel cubes across Q, Ka, Ku, X, and L bands.
key_parameters: L-band imaged in 16 channels (1-2 GHz), split into low (1-1.4 GHz) and high (1.5-1.9 GHz) sub-bands; X-band split into 46 channels across 2 GHz; Ka-band split into 24 channels across 8 GHz

recipe.goal: Derive physical properties of the sub-arcsecond ionized gas, pc-scale jet magnetic field, and 3D jet/disk orientation
recipe.method: Compute volume emission measure (VEM), electron density, and ionized mass of feature J1 from its 36 GHz optically-thin free-free flux density; estimate equipartition magnetic field of the pc-scale jet from its 1.6 GHz surface brightness; infer 3D jet and inner accretion disk orientation angles from PA and radial velocity signs.
key_parameters: J1 36 GHz integrated flux ~ 0.2 mJy; J1 dimensions 0.2'' x 0.02'' x 0.02''; jet diameter ~ 2'', 1.6 GHz surface brightness ~ 0.2 mJy beam^-1
assumptions: Galactic center distance d = 8 kpc; nominal electron temperature Te = 10^4 K; optically-thin thermal bremsstrahlung for J1 at 36 GHz
Equipartition between electrons and protons with an E^-2 electron energy spectrum between 10 MeV and 100 GeV
Jet emerges perpendicular to the equatorial plane of the inner accretion flow

score_reason: Archival ALMA and VLA project codes are clearly identified and the spectral window equalization and image-plane continuum subtraction procedures are described step-by-step, but key interferometric imaging and self-calibration parameters (robust weighting, solint, cell size) are omitted and there are minor numerical inconsistencies between text and figure captions regarding line-free channel ranges.
rediscovery_reason: Both ALMA datasets (2015.A.00021.S and 2011.0.00887.S) are public in the ALMA archive, the target position and aperture sizes are explicit, and the core spectroscopic result (confirming the +/-500 km/s double peak and testing the -2500/+4000 km/s excess under different continuum window assumptions) is a well-defined quantitative target.
